Subject: [URGENT] Production 5xx spike & tail latency on inference endpoints

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We’re seeing a sustained surge of 5xx errors and tail latencies above 400ms across our inference calls since ~08:50 PDT. Error rate peaked at ~12% for the critical checkout route. This is impacting live traffic for two of our regions and hitting SLA thresholds.

Quick details:
- First observed: 2026-10-02 08:50 PDT
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (primary), /v1/embeddings (secondary)
- Error type: HTTP 502 and 504 responses, occasional 500s
- Approx traffic: ~250 RPS during the spike; normal is ~80 RPS

We rotated on our side and confirmed no code deploys or app changes. Sable NOC suspects a gateway/proxy or upstream route problem. Can you triage and confirm if this is on Redwood’s forwarding/proxy side or something upstream of your edge?

We’re open to an immediate rollback to a previous routing profile if that helps. Please advise next steps; we need a timeline for mitigation and whether an exec is required.

Subject: Re: [URGENT] Production 5xx spike & tail latency on inference endpoints

TL;DR initial findings point to transient DNS resolution delays and proxy worker saturation on our egress nodes serving Sable’s VPC-peered region. Packet captures and proxy histograms attached.

What I see so far:
- Between 08:48–09:18 PDT: elevated DNS latency to Sable’s resolver (median 120ms -> 800ms for some queries). That correlates with bursts of 502/504 at the proxy layer.
- Proxy side: worker queue depth spiked and we observed CPU steal on the egress hosts servicing that peering group. Several proxy threads returned 502 under queue pressure.
- No recent code deploys in the last 48h on our edge.
- RTT to Sable VPC peer looked fine, but DNS timeouts caused retries and buffering that amplified latency.

Immediate mitigation performed (09:05–09:30):
- Increased proxy worker pool + temporarily disabled connection pooling on those nodes (reduced tail but not fully resolved).
- Added an emergency fallback route to a different peering region (started 09:22) which dropped observed 5xx rate by ~60%.

Attachments: sable_packet_capture_1002.pcap, proxy_histograms_1002.png

Next steps I recommend:
1) Work with Sable to check their resolver TTLs and transient load on their VPC peering endpoints.
2) Add more egress capacity to that peering group and tune DNS client timeouts.
3) For a durable fix consider pinning a cached resolver inside our VPC or using a secondary authoritative path.

I’ll continue to monitor and will push a short RCA doc after stabilization.

–Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

We attached the packet capture from our edge and our internal DNS logs (sable_packet_capture_1002.pcap, sable_error_logs_1002.zip). Appreciate the quick fallback route and capacity increase you applied — that helped while we adjusted our side.
